description:
One-shot operator-only backfill that populates the `session_ledger__session_source_kind` junction for pre-migration session groups. SQL-lockdown list_sessions slice: the junction `(canonical_session_id, source_kind)` — one row per distinct source_kind in a canonical session's `(vendor, external_session_id)` group — backs `list_sessions`' source_kind filter as a read-then-route (`query_state(junction, {source_kind: K})` → canonical ids → `query_state(session, {id: ANY})`), replacing the EXISTS-over-canonical-group subquery. `upsert_session` maintains the junction on the ingest attach-path for every NEW session, but the junction table starts EMPTY — so until this verb runs, `list_sessions(source_kind=K)` returns `[]` for every session that predates the migration.

Properties. (1) Idempotent + additive: each `(canonical_session_id, source_kind)` is an `upsert_state` DO-NOTHING on the UNIQUE pair, so a re-run inserts nothing new and it is non-destructive — no `confirm` gate (unlike the destructive repair verbs). (2) Race-free with ongoing ingest: new sessions self-populate via the attach-path and DO-NOTHING absorbs any overlap, so no importer-poll pause is needed. (3) Fail-loud: a session whose `(vendor, external_session_id)` group has NO canonical row (a duplicate-/orphaned-canonical anomaly) or whose `source_id` resolves to no live `__source` raises `LedgerRepositoryError` — RUN `lift_canonical_pointer_for_duplicate_sessions` FIRST so every group has exactly one canonical. (4) Bounded memory: a source-kind map + a canonical-id-by-group map (sources are few; one entry per canonical session) + an `id`-keyset session scan. Siblings share their canonical's `(vendor, external_session_id)`, so every member maps to its group's canonical and contributes its source's kind.

When to use. Run once after the list_sessions schema adoption (the junction table + the new ingest attach-path land together) to populate historical groups; run AFTER `lift_canonical_pointer_for_duplicate_sessions`. Re-run to confirm convergence — a clean run returns `junction_rows_written` 0.

This verb is `is_discoverable=False` — the model cannot find it via process_search and never proposes it. Operator-only via the operator bridge.
embedding_description: Operator-only one-shot ledger backfill: populate the session_source_kind junction (canonical_session_id, source_kind) for pre-migration session groups so list_sessions' source_kind filter finds historical sessions (the ingest attach-path maintains it for new sessions). Idempotent DO-NOTHING (no confirm gate), fail-loud on a group with no canonical (run lift_canonical_pointer_for_duplicate_sessions first) or a missing source, id-keyset paging, race-free with ingest. Returns sessions_scanned + junction_rows_written.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Backfill counts. `sessions_scanned` is the number of `__session` rows visited (id-keyset paged); `junction_rows_written` is the number of NEW (canonical_session_id, source_kind) pairs inserted this run (0 on a converged ledger — re-run to confirm completeness).
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: After a run, re-issue `list_sessions` with a `source_kind` filter and confirm pre-migration sessions now appear. Re-run this verb to confirm `junction_rows_written` is 0 (converged). If it raises `LedgerRepositoryError` about a group with no canonical, run `lift_canonical_pointer_for_duplicate_sessions` first, then re-run this backfill.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Two bounded maps (source_kind by source id; canonical id by (vendor, external_session_id) group) + an id-keyset scan of `__session`; per session, one `upsert_state` DO-NOTHING into `session_source_kind` keyed (canonical_session_id, source_kind).
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: LedgerRepositoryError: either a session's `(vendor, external_session_id)` group has no canonical row (duplicate-/orphaned-canonical anomaly — the backfill stops rather than orphan the group) or a session references a missing `__source`, or the state_service rejected a read/upsert. Possible causes: `lift_canonical_pointer_for_duplicate_sessions` not yet run, schema not yet adopted (the junction table absent), a dangling `__session.source_id`.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: Run `lift_canonical_pointer_for_duplicate_sessions` to resolve duplicate canonicals FIRST. Confirm the list_sessions schema (the junction table) is adopted. For a dangling source, reconcile via `list_sources` before re-running. The backfill is idempotent, so a re-run after fixing the anomaly resumes cleanly (existing pairs are skipped).
